name: Sleater-Kinney
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: Two guitarists from Olympia named their band after a freeway exit, skipped the bass, and sang their own breakup on record. A breakdown before a Brussels show stopped them in 2006; eight years later they announced a record they had already made.

eras.title: Two guitars, no bass, one exit off I-5
eras.text: Corin Tucker of Heavens to Betsy and Carrie Brownstein of Excuse 17 start Sleater-Kinney in Olympia as a side project. Two records in two years on the queercore label Chainsaw Records make them critics' favorites before they have a steady drummer.

years.h: An Olympia side project, named for a freeway exit
years.p: Corin Tucker has just graduated from The Evergreen State College, where Carrie Brownstein is still a student. They take the name from Sleater Kinney Road in Lacey, the turnoff at I-5 exit 108.
years.xp: The road is named for two 19th-century families, the Sleaters and Henry and Martha Kinney, who lived in Olympia's South Bay neighborhood.

years.h: Their last night in Australia becomes the debut album
years.p: Tucker and Brownstein, a couple at the time, record the songs that make up their first record.

years.h: The Australian tapes come out as Sleater-Kinney
years.p: Chainsaw Records releases the first album, with [[Lora MacFarlane|15ab5023-3b1c-4bdf-afe5-184932a6edfb]] behind the kit.

years.h: Call the Doctor: three weeks to write, four days to record
years.p: [[John Goodmanson|6f62dbe4-701c-4c4b-a204-420996982e9f]] produces it for Chainsaw. It ranks third in the Village Voice's 1996 critics' poll, and sells 6,000 copies by March 1997 and 60,000 in the US by 2015.
years.xp:
There's no bass player. Tucker said two guitars gave them room to write lines that go back and forth. She wrote out of frustration with work and with how society makes people consumerized and commodified.

AllMusic called it pure, undiluted punk. Rolling Stone later put it at No. 49 among the greatest albums of the 1990s.

years.h: Spin outs Carrie Brownstein at 21
years.p: The magazine reports that Brownstein is bisexual and has been in a relationship with bandmate Corin Tucker. Brownstein later describes herself more broadly as queer.

years.h: Lora MacFarlane's Australian visa runs out
years.p: The drummer leaves soon after Call the Doctor comes out. Misty Farrell and Toni Gogin also drum for the band in its early years.

eras.title: A drummer who knew the Stones
eras.text: Janet Weiss of Quasi sees them play, joins, and brings a drummer's range that takes in the Stones and Lightnin' Hopkins as well as punk. Sleater-Kinney moves to Kill Rock Stars, digs the studio out of a Seattle snowstorm, and makes the record that takes them worldwide.

years.src: Wikipedia: Janet Weiss · Wikipedia: Dig Me Out
years.h: Janet Weiss watches a show and ends up in the band
years.p: Weiss, drummer of Portland's [[Quasi|3df29542-402a-49a5-ae1f-82f936184b3b]], becomes the fourth drummer in Sleater-Kinney after seeing them play. She stays ten years, then five more.
years.xp:
Weiss started drumming in The Furies at 22, after one lesson and two weeks of practice. She moved to Portland in 1989 and formed Quasi with Sam Coomes, her former husband, in 1993.

Tucker told Addicted to Noise that Weiss became the bottom end and the solidness the band had always wanted. Brownstein has called her "one of the most musically intelligent people I know."

yt: Dig Me Out record release show, 1997
years.h: Dig Me Out is named for a snowed-in studio
years.p: The band records it in eight days at John and Stu's Place in Seattle over winter 1996-97, digging the studio out of the snow. Kill Rock Stars releases it, and it lands at No. 4 in the Pazz & Jop poll.
years.xp:
Producer [[John Goodmanson|6f62dbe4-701c-4c4b-a204-420996982e9f]] noted that Call the Doctor took four days; the new label paid for twice that. Robert Christgau wrote that the band was so confident of its ability to please that it couldn't stop.

Rolling Stone ranked it No. 189 on its 2020 list of the greatest albums of all time.

yt: Full set, CBGB, New York, May 15, 1997
years.h: Tucker and Brownstein sing their own breakup on One More Hour
years.p: The Dig Me Out song is about the end of Corin Tucker and Carrie Brownstein's romantic relationship. They sing it together.
years.xp: The band toured the record that spring. A full set from CBGB in New York, May 15, 1997, is on YouTube.

years.h: The Hot Rock starts the push toward the mainstream
years.p: It is the first of three albums, with All Hands on the Bad One and One Beat to follow, that move Sleater-Kinney toward a bigger audience.

years.h: Corin Tucker marries Lance Bangs in Iceland
years.p: Bangs, a filmmaker, and Tucker go on to have two children.

years.h: All Hands on the Bad One arrives, still on Kill Rock Stars
years.p: The fifth album keeps building the band's audience.

eras.title: Arenas, and the loudest record yet
eras.text: Critics reach for superlatives, Pearl Jam takes the band into arenas, and it answers with the loudest record it ever made, on a new label with a new producer.

years.h: Greil Marcus puts a title on them
years.p: The critic Greil Marcus gives Sleater-Kinney the line in 2001. Robert Christgau goes plainer: one of the essential rock groups of the early 2000s.

years.h: One Beat is their last record for Kill Rock Stars
years.p: The sixth album finishes the move toward bigger rooms.

years.h: Pearl Jam takes them into the arenas
years.p: Starting in 2003, Sleater-Kinney opens many North American arena shows for [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]]. The band later credits the experience with inspiring its next album.
years.xp: The ties lasted. On November 29, 2013, Sleater-Kinney members joined Pearl Jam, along with Scott McCaughey and Peter Buck, for a Neil Young cover.

years.cap: Sleater-Kinney live on The Woods tour, October 2005
years.h: Sub Pop puts out The Woods, their heaviest record
years.p: [[Dave Fridmann|6b09687f-72de-4337-9a0b-da8f6248ce7c]] produces, and the band records mostly live at Tarbox Road Studios in Cassadaga, New York. It is their first album for Sub Pop.
years.xp:
Let's Call It Love (11:01) and Night Light were cut as a single 15-minute take after Brownstein noticed they were in the same key. Only vocals and a few guitars were overdubbed.

It reached No. 80 on the Billboard 200 and sold 94,000 US copies by 2015. Q gave it two stars; Rolling Stone later put it at No. 72 of the decade.

eras.title: The breakdown in Brussels
eras.text: Sleater-Kinney ended at a peak, and it wasn't planned. Brownstein told the whole story nine years later in her memoir.

years.cap: Tucker, Brownstein and Weiss backstage at SXSW, Austin, March 2006
years.big: Two days of shingles, ten years of band
years.h: Brownstein breaks down in Brussels, and the band stops
years.p: Two days before a European tour, Carrie Brownstein gets shingles and is kept apart from Janet Weiss, who never had chickenpox. Before the show at Le Botanique, she breaks down in front of Corin Tucker and Weiss.
years.xp:
Brownstein says the shingles came from anxiety, and being isolated from her bandmates made her mental health worse. Tucker was also exhausted by touring and wanted time with her family.

Brownstein told the story in her 2015 memoir Hunger Makes Me a Modern Girl.

years.cap: Carrie Brownstein at Lollapalooza, Chicago, August 2006
years.h: Sleater-Kinney announces an indefinite hiatus
years.p: The statement says there are "no plans for future tours or recordings." The band then plays Lollapalooza, its last major public show.

years.h: Portland's Crystal Ballroom is the last stop before the break
years.p: Sleater-Kinney plays its final concert of the first run in Portland, Oregon.

eras.title: Three people, three other lives
eras.text: With the band on ice, Weiss drums for Stephen Malkmus, Tucker goes solo, and Brownstein starts a band and a TV show that make her famous far outside music.

years.cap: Janet Weiss on the kit with Quasi
years.h: Weiss keeps drumming, now for Stephen Malkmus
years.p: Janet Weiss plays on [[Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks|98e4bf9e-9e33-4f07-9962-f7c1c2d773ba]]' Real Emotional Trash (2008) and Mirror Traffic (2011), leaving before the second album's tour.

years.h: Corin Tucker goes solo with 1,000 Years
years.p: Kill Rock Stars releases it, with Unwound's Sara Lund and Seth Lorinczi of [[Circus Lupus|01b418b2-5e47-4ce2-9144-ad7d35214103]] backing her. Kill My Blues follows in 2012.

years.h: Portlandia premieres on IFC
years.p: Carrie Brownstein and [[Fred Armisen|b1bad7e7-18fd-4c1d-9a64-66c3696209ac]]'s sketch show runs until March 2018 and wins Emmy and Peabody awards.

years.cap: Janet Weiss drumming with Wild Flag, March 2011
years.h: Wild Flag puts Brownstein and Weiss in a band with Mary Timony
years.p: With [[Mary Timony|d9c8dc3c-15b8-40d5-8153-ae9214aeef55]] of [[Helium|573510d6-bb5d-4d07-b0aa-ea6afe39e28d]] and Rebecca Cole of the Minders, [[Wild Flag|4473e47b-81bb-47af-8cb0-1cad6f68d8bc]] releases its only album on Merge Records. By 2014 the band is inactive.
years.xp: Brownstein revealed the lineup in September 2010. Looking back, she said: "We had a fun run... but all the logistics started seeming not quite worth it."

eras.title: The secret record
eras.text: Sleater-Kinney recorded a comeback album before telling anyone, reached No. 18 with it, then lost the drummer who had defined the band.

years.h: Sleater-Kinney announces No Cities to Love, already made
years.p: The band recorded in secret, mostly at Tiny Telephone in San Francisco with [[John Goodmanson|6f62dbe4-701c-4c4b-a204-420996982e9f]]. The Start Together vinyl box set comes out the same year.
years.xp: The announcement also came with a 2015 tour covering North America and western Europe.

years.h: Sub Pop puts No Cities to Love online early, by mistake
years.p: The label's slip streams the album weeks before its January 20 release.

years.src: Wikipedia: No Cities to Love · Wikipedia: Sleater-Kinney
years.h: No Cities to Love lands at No. 18 to near-universal praise
years.p: Sub Pop releases it. The New York Times' Jon Pareles calls it the first great album of 2015; Stereogum's Tom Breihan calls them the greatest rock band of the past two decades.
years.xp: The title track's video features Andy Samberg, Sarah Silverman, Brie Larson and Gerard Way. The March 20 show at La Cigale in Paris became the band's first live album, Live in Paris, in January 2017.

years.h: Brownstein writes the band's story in Hunger Makes Me a Modern Girl
years.p: The 2015 memoir covers the 2006 breakdown that ended the first run.

years.h: Annie Clark, as St. Vincent, will produce album nine
years.p: Sleater-Kinney announces that [[St. Vincent|5334edc0-5faf-4ca5-b1df-000de3e1f752]] is producing its ninth album, recorded in Portland.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Center Won't Hold · Wikipedia: Janet Weiss
years.h: Janet Weiss leaves a month before The Center Won't Hold
years.p: Weiss announces it on Twitter. She said Corin Tucker and Carrie Brownstein had made clear she would no longer be a creative equal, only the drummer.
years.xp: Weiss said the roles within the band had changed and she didn't want to play songs live she hadn't helped create. She had been in the band since 1996 and played on every album from Dig Me Out on.

years.h: The Center Won't Hold peaks at No. 27
years.p: St. Vincent produces and Mom + Pop releases it. It reaches No. 27 on the Billboard 200 and No. 2 on the alternative chart.

years.cap: Sleater-Kinney at the Palladium, Los Angeles, November 2019
years.h: Angie Boylan drums at Hopscotch, the first show without Janet Weiss
years.p: Sleater-Kinney plays North Carolina's Hopscotch Music Festival with its new drummer.

eras.title: Down to two
eras.text: Down to the founding pair, Sleater-Kinney kept making records fast. Then a family tragedy reshaped the next one.

years.h: Path of Wellness is the first album as a duo
years.p: Worry With You leads the way, released May 11. The band tours with [[Wilco|9e53f84d-ef44-4c16-9677-5fd4d78cbd7d]] that summer.

years.h: Brownstein's mother and stepfather die in a car crash in Italy
years.p: Half of the next album, Little Rope, is written before the accident and half after.

years.cap: Carrie Brownstein at the Roundhouse, London
years.h: Little Rope is made with grief in the room
years.p: [[John Congleton|6da4067f-e6ce-49b6-925c-56e017075038]] produces in Portland, and Loma Vista releases it. Pitchfork calls it the band's sturdiest rock record since No Cities to Love.
